### LOW: External prefix\-cache volume option changes the T\-041 at\-rest threat model \(TTL purge, volume trust\)
[CHANGELOG\.md:5](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/5e8ee162f9900a959c82a113d74148921bba5f7d/CHANGELOG.md#L5) · A-001, T-041

CHANGELOG\.md line 5 adds \`darkbloom cache set \-\-directory \.\.\.\`, which moves encrypted SSD prefix\-cache files to an operator\-chosen external volume, and pins the volume UUID\. T\-041 assumes a single on\-box root \(darkbloom/kv3\)\. It also assumes the 30\-minute sliding TTL, the opportunistic sweep and the disk budget bound how long DBK3 artifacts exist\. If the external disk is unmounted or replaced, the provider 'refuses \.\.\. without falling back', so the sweep cannot run\. Encrypted files then persist on a removable, portable device well past the TTL\. The HMAC\-named files also keep leaking file count, sizes and mtimes\. The KEK stays on the Mac, which limits content exposure; the KEK wipe remains the crypto purge\. The threat model does not cover this new at\-rest location, the TTL\-expiry gap for detached media, or the trust placed in the volume UUID and 'encryption required' check\. Update T\-041 and TB\-007 to cover external roots\. State that TTL and LRU purge need the volume mounted, and that the KEK wipe is the only purge for detached media\. Confirm the encryption check cannot be bypassed by a user\-controlled mount\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Relocatable cache directory breaks the TTL\-bounded at\-rest claim in the threat model
[docs/architecture/security/encryption\.md:185](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/5e8ee162f9900a959c82a113d74148921bba5f7d/docs/architecture/security/encryption.md#L185) · A-001, T-016, T-041

The new section lets operators point the encrypted prefix cache at an arbitrary directory, including an external or removable SSD\. It also says that after a location switch the old ciphertext is never swept or securely erased\. T\-041 and its mitigations \(SSD at\-rest window bounded by a 30\-minute sliding TTL and an available\-disk/2 LRU budget, 20 GiB reserve, KEK wipe as purge\) assume one on\-box store that maintenance fully controls\. After a switch, or if the operator keeps a detachable disk, stale DBK3 files persist indefinitely\. Their file sizes, timestamps, model and layout binding, and HMAC tags stay observable to an adversarial provider operator or whoever holds the disk\. The doc also admits that a malicious controller can retain ciphertext, replay still\-valid ciphertext, or defeat the filesystem\-UUID pin by cloning it\. The result is a new at\-rest surface \(removable or untrusted peripherals\) and a new replay and rollback surface that T\-041, T\-016 and TB\-003 do not cover\. Their disk\-budget, TTL and purge mitigations are also silent on which volume they apply to\. Fix: update T\-041 and TB\-003 to cover a configurable payload location, orphaned ciphertext after a switch, and external\-controller replay/retention\. Consider sweeping or TTL\-purging the previous directory on a switch, binding the freshness or TTL check to a Mac\-local ledger, and scoping the budget and reserve to the selected volume\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Threat model lacks coverage for relocatable external\-volume provider cache storage
[docs/architecture/security/encryption\.md:198](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/5e8ee162f9900a959c82a113d74148921bba5f7d/docs/architecture/security/encryption.md#L198) · T-012, T-016, T-041

The new 'Provider cache storage' section describes a \`darkbloom cache set \-\-directory\` feature that moves encrypted KV\-cache payloads to external APFS volumes\. Its trust checks are a pinned filesystem UUID, ownership and flag checks, and an APFS\-encryption requirement\. The doc itself says these are not peripheral attestation\. A malicious or cloned controller can defeat the UUID pin, retain ciphertext, delete or replay still\-valid ciphertext, and supply traffic\-analysis metadata \(sizes, times, model/layout binding\)\. Switching locations also leaves stale ciphertext in the old location with no secure erase\. The canonical model covers the SSD cache under T\-041 and disk\-fill DoS under T\-016\. It has no threat or mitigation for removable or untrusted storage, UUID\-clone spoofing, replay of valid ciphertext, or orphaned ciphertext after relocation\. Trigger: an operator, or an adversarial provider, points the cache at an attacker\-influenced volume\. Impact: availability and metadata leakage, and possible replay of cache blocks within the TTL\. Fix: add a TB\-003/T\-041 threat entry covering relocatable cache storage, with the documented mitigations and residuals \(authenticated encryption, TTL and tenant binding, no peripheral attestation, no secure erase on relocation\)\. Confirm the code matches the doc's claims\. The code was not supplied in this batch\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

findings.detail: The new section documents `darkbloom cache set --directory`, which can put DBK3 payloads on an external APFS volume. It also admits that TTL/LRU deletion needs the volume mounted. Detached or inaccessible media can keep ciphertext and metadata indefinitely, and switching locations leaves old ciphertext behind. Restart freshness is seeded from mtimes, so a malicious disk can replay valid files and metadata. A filesystem-UUID pin can be defeated by cloning the UUID. T-041 and its mitigations still say the at-rest window is bounded by a 30-minute sliding TTL and a box-wide LRU budget. They name `darkbloom/kv3` as the only on-disk root, and describe KEK wipe as the purge. Nothing in them covers an operator-chosen, possibly removable store. A malicious operator or enclosure controller retains ciphertext plus visible size, time and model metadata past the TTL (ADV-001). It can also replay still-valid files. Fix: update T-041 to add the selectable volume as a new at-rest surface with these residuals. Reword the TTL and LRU mitigations as 'while mounted'. Add the UUID-pin limitation and make the KEK wipe the only guaranteed purge. Add the cache-volume files named in the PR to its detection_hint and affected_files.
findings.title: T-041 at-rest window and purge claims do not cover relocatable or external cache volumes

findings.detail: docs/provider/cache-storage.md documents a new operator-selected external/separate volume for encrypted SSD prefix-cache payloads, which are derived from consumer prompts (A-001). The same page states that expiry cannot delete files on detached or previously selected disks, and that `--reset-directory` and re-selecting a disk leave old files in place. The result is a retention and exfiltration surface outside the internal disk. It consists of detached media, a volume-UUID pin, `provider.toml` as a trust anchor, and the operator's choice of removable hardware with unverified firmware. Visible threat-model text does not cover this. The T-041 cache entry was too large to inspect here, so I could not confirm whether it already covers it. The PR is docs-only, so I could not verify in code that payloads stay HMAC-keyed and encrypted with keys kept off the removable volume. Fix: add a TB-003/T-041 entry for external cache volumes with their residual risks (orphaned ciphertext, attacker-swapped volumes, a tampered `provider.toml` redirecting the cache, unlimited daily writes). Confirm in the implementing PR that keys never reside on the cache volume.
findings.title: Removable-disk cache option is not reflected in the threat model (A-001 / T-041)

findings.detail:
The patch documents `cache.directory` and `cache.volume_uuid`, which move the encrypted SSD prefix-cache payloads to an operator-chosen absolute directory (the `darkbloom/kv3` child) on a possibly external or removable volume. It also documents `cache.daily_write_gb`, where `0` means an unlimited write budget. T-041 and its detection_hint still describe a fixed on-disk root (`darkbloom/kv3`) and a fixed-posture disk policy. That policy uses an available-disk/2 budget, a 20 GiB pre-write reserve and a 750 GB/day write cap. The model does not cover the following changes in at-rest exposure:
- Cache files can sit on a volume that can be detached or shared, or that has different permissions.
- The volume-UUID check happens only when the directory is opened, so it does not cover the cache path becoming unavailable later.
- An unlimited write budget removes the SSD wear/DoS bound.
HMAC-named, AES-GCM encrypted files and the TTL still apply. T-041 should be updated to list the configured root and volume binding as part of the purge, TTL and disk-budget surface, and to state whether the free-space reserve and TTL sweep apply on the configured volume.
findings.title: T-041 needs updating for operator-configurable SSD cache root and volume binding
